document.title: Terrorism: Historical Background of the Islamic Army, And Bin Ladin's Move from Afghanistan to Sudan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: Historical background of the Islamic Army and bin Ladin's move from Afghanistan to Sudan. Source: 9/11 Commission Report, Chapter 2, Endnotes 25, 31, 35, 36; Chapter 4, Endnote 3.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Islamic extremist financier; founder of al-Qaida during the Afghan war; led the Islamic Army in Sudan

mentions.quote: DURING THE AFGHAN WAR, USAMA BIN LADIN CREATED THE ISLAMIC EXTREMIST ORGANIZATION AL-QAIDA FROM AMONG LOYAL MUJAHIDIN IN AFGHANISTAN.
IN 1989, BIN LADIN MOVED AL-QAIDA TO SUDAN, AT THE BEHEST OF THE NATIONAL ISLAMIC FRONT, AND CHANGED THE NAME TO THE ISLAMIC ARMY.
BIN LADIN AGREED TO PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE SUDANESE CIVIL DEFENSE AND TO BUILD THE "CHALLENGE ROAD" FROM KHARTOUM TO PORT SUDAN

organizations.name: al-Qaida
organizations.notes: Established by Bin Ladin during the Afghan war to facilitate movement of Islamic extremists into and out of Afghanistan; moved to Sudan in 1989 and renamed the Islamic Army; the term al-Qaida reportedly no longer made sense once the worldwide network was sought.

organizations.name: Islamic Army
organizations.notes: Name given to al-Qaida after its move to Sudan; Bin Ladin defined its Koranic basis and intent to use violence for Islamic goals.

organizations.name: National Islamic Front
organizations.notes: Came to power in Sudan in 1989; asked Bin Ladin to establish his organization there; its most immediate concern was the civil war in the south.

organizations.name: Government of Sudan
organizations.notes: With the NIF provided a receptive environment and personnel supporting Islamic Army activities.

organizations.name: Sudanese Civil Defense
organizations.notes: Bin Ladin agreed to fund it.

places.name: Afghanistan
places.significance: Where al-Qaida was created during the Afghan war.

places.name: Sudan
places.significance: Bin Ladin's base after 1989, hosted by the NIF.

relationships.quote: BIN LADIN AGREED TO ESTABLISH HIS AL-QAIDA/ISLAMIC ARMY IN SUDAN, AT THE BEHEST OF THE NIF.

sources_cited: CIA Information Report, 26 November 1996 (not finally evaluated intelligence)
key_claims: Bin Ladin created al-Qaida during the Afghan war to facilitate movement of extremists into and out of Afghanistan.
In 1989 Bin Ladin moved al-Qaida to Sudan at the behest of the NIF and renamed it the Islamic Army.
The NIF and Sudanese government provided a receptive environment and personnel in return for Bin Ladin-provided infrastructure.
Bin Ladin agreed to fund Sudanese civil defense and build the Challenge Road from Khartoum to Port Sudan in exchange for land.
Bin Ladin and committee members were already discussing violence as a means to achieve Islamic goals.
